story: Kanye West had used Auto-Tune on background vocals for The College Dropout in 2004, but not for lead vocals. In 2008, working on remixes of Lil Wayne's "Lollipop" and Young Jeezy's "Put On", he took to it, and T-Pain coached him. After his mother Donda died in November 2007 and his engagement to Alexis Phifer ended in April 2008, West recorded 808s & Heartbreak in September and October 2008 in Burbank, California and Honolulu. He flew in Kid Cudi, whose 2008 mixtape A Kid Named Cudi he admired, and Cudi co-wrote four songs. West felt rapping could not carry what he felt, so he mostly sang, through Auto-Tune, over the Roland TR-808 drum machine in minor keys. Hip-hop fans and some rappers mocked him for becoming "sappy". Drake's producer Noah "40" Shebib named the album as an influence on the mixtape So Far Gone, released in February 2009 and launched with a party in Toronto. Kid Cudi followed with Man on the Moon: The End of Day in 2009. The album is credited with starting emo rap; B.o.B and Childish Gambino turned to introspection after it, and Juice Wrld and Lil Uzi Vert later named it as an influence.

disagreements: Origin: our record says Los Angeles and Toronto. 808s & Heartbreak was recorded 'at Glenwood Studios in [[Burbank, California]] and Avex Recording Studio in [[Honolulu|Honolulu, Hawaii]]' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/808s_%26_Heartbreak?action=raw); Kanye West is not described there as an LA artist. Toronto is supported only through Drake's So Far Gone.
'Melodic rap' has no article of its own on English Wikipedia (it redirects to Pop rap); the 808s & Heartbreak article credits the album with 'pioneering the [[emo rap]]' instead.
Window end 2014: the sources trace the line on into the late 2010s (Juice Wrld, Lil Uzi Vert).
notes: Home language English. Built from the 808s & Heartbreak and So Far Gone articles; the Pop rap article (redirect target) was fetched but not used.
